internal_decisions: Names are untrusted, so upload_path also raises ValueError for NUL bytes, absolute names, and names resolving to the base itself or outside it (.. escape). Inner .. that stays inside is allowed.
Used os.path.abspath + commonpath (no filesystem access, base need not exist; symlinks not resolved).
not_checked: Symlink traversal inside base is not handled (no filesystem access by design)

internal_decisions: Token format: base64url(file_id).expires.base64url(HMAC-SHA256 of the first two parts)
Signature is checked before the expiry is parsed, so malformed or tampered tokens always end as InvalidToken
Non-ASCII or non-str tokens raise InvalidToken
LIKE with ESCAPE '\' and escaped %, _ and backslash for literal matching
Results sorted in Python (binary order), so uppercase sorts before lowercase
Commit after each write so the catalogue works on a plain connection

plan: Baseline: tests (22) and acceptance (16) all green.
Contracts: no cross-module dependencies (WPs independent), so contract checks reduced to each module's own signature edges.
Edge cases: path traversal/NUL/absolute names; token tampering, non-str tokens, dotted ids, non-ASCII ids; catalogue backslash, quote, SQL injection, owner case, duplicates (all pass).
Acceptance: covered by acceptance/, not duplicated.
Regression/non-functional: discarded (no prior code, no performance requirements).
D1 test (test_d1_verify_rejects_empty_secret) is red on purpose.

defects.section: 6 (tokens: verify only accepts tokens issued with the same secret; secret is non-empty bytes)
defects.repro: verify(b'', 'ZjE.5000.' + _sign(b'', 'ZjE.5000'), 1) returns 'f1'. issue refuses an empty secret, so this token was never produced by issue, yet verify accepts it. A non-bytes secret (str/None) gives TypeError, not InvalidToken or ValueError.
defects.fix: In verify, raise ValueError if secret is not non-empty bytes, as issue does.
defects.if_skipped: A caller that misconfigures an empty secret accepts tokens anyone can forge, with no error to flag it.

gaps: Symlink escapes in upload_path are not tested: the contract is lexical and nothing is written to disk.
No concurrency tests for Catalogue: the contract says nothing about threads.
Non-ASCII input for the catalogue is outside the contract, so it is not tested.

advisory.problem: Tampering is tested only at the end of the token (last character, truncation, appended 'x'). Nothing changes the expiry or file id part. A token that signs only the id, or only part of the payload, would still pass. The 'carries the expiry' and 'any string not produced by issue' guarantees are only partly covered.
advisory.evidence: An implementation that puts the expiry in the clear, outside the signature, passes all token tests. Editing the expiry in a token would then extend its life.

advisory.problem: Round-trip and expiry tests use only the id 'file-42' and expiry 2000. Nothing shows that the id and expiry come from the arguments.
advisory.evidence: An implementation that returns 'file-42' for every validly signed token passes. An implementation that hardcodes the expiry check at 2000 passes too.

advisory.problem: test_plain_name asserts that a fixed path under /tmp does not exist. It depends on the environment and fails if something creates that directory.
advisory.evidence: Creating /tmp/vault-acceptance-missing-base on the machine makes the test fail whatever the implementation does.

advisory.problem: The AC-007 test covers only the three listed inputs. Other whitespace ids such as a tab or newline, and non-ASCII ids, are not tested.
advisory.evidence: An implementation that rejects only the space character and the empty string passes.
